attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is valid for EF+SAT_U^{occ}. It is blocked for full EF+SAT_U by the missing extraction lemma from real SAT semantic derivations to syntactic row forcing; full EF may use formula structure in a nonrelativizing way that private occurrence-label spoofing does not preserve.
steps: Define U_N={(x,j):x in {0,1}^N, j<=M_N} and replace each SAT(G_N(x,j)) by an independent occurrence label a_{x,j}.

Parse an accepted occurrence-local transcript pi into Q_pi by collecting every queried occurrence, every locally derived equation, and every explicit row-parity tag; define ForcedRows(Q_pi) as rows whose parity is fixed under all completions of Q_pi.
Prove parser invariance by induction on the EF+SAT_U^{occ} derivation: each rule depends only on premises already in Q_pi, so preserving Q_pi preserves acceptance.
For every unforced row choose a private completion making xor_j a_{x,j}=0 while preserving Q_pi; forced rows keep their Q_pi-determined parity.
The spoofed carrier H_{A^0} is supported on R=ForcedRows(Q_pi), so a nonuniform circuit hardwires R and uses O(N)-size equality tests to patch those rows, with total size S_Q+O(|R|N).
If pi is functionally sound for the claimed lower bound s_N, then H_{A^0} must have circuit complexity greater than s_N; the patch circuit contradicts this whenever S_Q+O(|R|N)<s_N.

Conclude that any valid occurrence-local functional certificate at the N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} threshold must force N^{epsilon-o(1)} complete rows, unless it is nonfunctional, nonconstructive, too large, or uses real SAT semantics outside EF+SAT_U^{occ}.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a route-specific no-go for a proof-mediated hardness-magnification certificate, not a lower bound for H_N^SAT and not a proof of P != NP. It certifies a falsifier for occurrence-local functional certificates and identifies the exact full-EF boundary.

assumptions: Generator G_N is available to the carrier circuit with size N^{rho+o(1)}, and the SAT-query length is beta=0, namely L_N=(log N)^d.

Psys=EF+SAT_U^{occ} is occurrence-local: rule validity is invariant under arbitrary replacements of occurrence labels outside Q_pi, with no appeal to real formula semantics except through listed occurrence labels.
Functional soundness: an accepted certificate for C(H_A)>s_N must be valid for every occurrence-label completion A consistent with Q_pi, not only for the real SAT label vector.
The proof-size/parser overhead satisfies S_Q<s_N-O(|R|N); otherwise the certificate is too large to support the barely-superlinear source claim.
Circuit model is nonuniform Boolean circuits over N-bit source inputs; a row patch for a listed x uses an equality test of size O(N).
definitions: source object: H_N^SAT(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)) on N-bit source rows x, with M_N<=N^{q+o(1)} and generated formulas of length L_N=(log N)^d.
target object: a scoped no-go/extraction theorem for Psys=EF+SAT_U^{occ} certificates that claim C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} as input to beta=0 magnification.

controlled interface: occurrence labels a_{x,j} replace SAT(G_N(x,j)); a transcript pi is parsed to Q_pi=(T_pi,row-tags,local equations) and can inspect only these labels through occurrence-local rules.

target-preserving condition: the theorem preserves the beta=0 transfer only for q,rho<1+epsilon and treats private occurrence-label spoofing as a falsifier of the certificate route, not as a circuit for real SAT.

ForcedRows(Q_pi) is the set of rows x whose parity xor_j a_{x,j} is fixed by Q_pi under all occurrence-label completions; in the atomic occurrence model this requires all row labels to be touched or an explicit locally derived row-parity tag.
S_Q is the size of the nonuniform circuit that evaluates the parsed finite object Q_pi and the spoofed default predicate; equality patching on E source rows costs O(EN) gates.

Let Q_pi be the parsed occurrence object, S_Q its evaluator cost, and R=ForcedRows(Q_pi). If S_Q+O(|R|N)<s_N, then pi is invalid under a private occurrence-label spoof. attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The proof is valid for strict occurrence-local EF+SAT_U^{occ} with row-view soundness. It is blocked for full EF+SAT_U because real formula syntax and SAT_U semantics may create dependencies not preserved by private occurrence-label perturbations.
steps: Fix strict EF+SAT_U^{occ}; replay pi and collect Q_pi, all cited occurrence bits, equality/copy links, and explicit row-XOR gates.
Compute cl_occ(Q_pi). Define ForcedRows(pi) as rows whose row-XOR symbol h_x is fixed in this closure; this is syntactic and independent of C(H_N^{SAT}).
Assume |R_pi| is small. Pick a decoy D_N of size S_D, e.g. constant zero or the best audited residual circuit.
Build A_Q: on forced rows set occurrence bits to the actual SAT values; on every unforced row preserve all bits seen by pi and set one remaining free occurrence bit so that the row XOR equals D_N(x).
Because V_N and every rule are occurrence-local, pi has exactly the same view under A_Q as under the actual SAT occurrence assignment; acceptance is invariant.
The induced function H_N^{A_Q} equals H_N^{SAT} only on R_pi and equals D_N off R_pi, so the sparse patch circuit has size at most S_D+c|R_pi|N.
Row-view soundness of the certificate says an accepted proof cannot exist for any completion whose induced function has circuit size <=T_N. Therefore c|R_pi|N+S_D>T_N.
For T_N=N^{1+epsilon} and S_D<=N^{1+eta}, eta<epsilon, this yields |R_pi|>=N^{epsilon-o(1)}.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a scoped route-level no-go/extraction theorem, not a proof of P != NP. Promotion needs the full parser boundary resolved, prior-art checked, and a proof-quality audit of row-view soundness versus ordinary soundness.

assumptions: N=2^n, M_N<=N^{q+o(1)}, formula length L_N=(log N)^d, and G_N is uniform with overhead N^{rho+o(1)}.
The target model is nonuniform Boolean circuits on n=log N inputs with size threshold T_N=N^{1+epsilon}.
Psys is the strict occurrence-local abstraction: real SAT formula equality, semantic satisfiability, and global EF extension variables are unavailable unless explicitly represented in Q_pi.
Closure completeness holds: if x is not in ForcedRows(pi), there is an occurrence completion preserving cl_occ(Q_pi) that flips the row XOR at x.
A decoy D_N on n inputs has circuit size S_D and can be imposed on every unforced row by setting one free occurrence bit in that row.
Sparse patching uses hardwired exceptional rows and costs at most c|R|N gates in the audited circuit model.
definitions: source object: EF+SAT_U^{occ} transcript pi accepted by a verifier V_N for H_N^{SAT}(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)) with private occurrence labels (x,j).
target object: scoped no-go/extraction theorem for claimed certificates of C(H_N^{SAT})>N^{1+epsilon} in the occurrence-local model.
controlled interface: parser pi -> Q_pi, occurrence closure cl_occ(Q_pi), ForcedRows(pi), spoof completion A_Q, and sparse patch circuit P_{D,R}.

target-preserving condition: the verifier and proof rules read only occurrence labels in Q_pi and declared local row-XOR gates, while the patch circuit preserves the same H_N length, generator G_N, and circuit-size threshold T_N.

Complete/forced row: x is forced when the row parity vector for (x,1),...,(x,M_N) is syntactically determined inside cl_occ(Q_pi); in the pure label-read subcase this requires all M_N labels or an explicit row-XOR gate.
Row-view soundness: no accepted transcript may remain accepted for an occurrence assignment A whose induced row function H_N^A has circuit size at most T_N.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Strict occurrence-local EF+SAT_U^{occ} row-forcing theorem: fix T_N=N^{1+epsilon}. If an accepted transcript pi is row-view sound for the beta-zero XOR carrier and the parser closure is complete for occurrence constraints, then either |ForcedRows(pi)| >= (T_N-S_D)/(cN) for every decoy circuit D of size S_D, or the same accepted view is a falsifier because it has a completion whose induced row function has circuit size below T_N. With S_D<=N^{1+eta}, eta<epsilon, sound certificates force N^{epsilon-o(1)} rows. This is valid only for the strict occurrence-local model, not full EF+SAT_U.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The parser and patch chain are theorem-shaped for EF+SAT_U^{occ}, but promotion needs a rule-by-rule proof that every accepted transcript either exposes row-parity binding clauses or is invariant under the private odd-row perturbation. Full EF+SAT_U also needs a separate extraction lemma from real SAT formula syntax to complete rows.
steps: Fix N and parse pi into Q_pi=(V_pi,E_pi,Cover_pi,Sem_pi); define D_pi by opening the labels used in the XOR row and define F_pi by syntactic row-parity binding clauses.

Use the adaptive-cover normal form to build an unrestricted circuit for D_pi: compute G_N, enumerate M_N=N^{q+o(1)} row queries, open labels through the cover, and XOR them, giving exponent max{rho,q+alpha_ad}.
Assume row-parity binding for all x notin F_pi. Then D_pi and H_N^SAT differ only on F_pi.
Patch the forced rows by a row-lookup correction circuit of size O(|F_pi|N), obtaining C(H_N^SAT)<=N^{max{rho,q+alpha_ad,1+f}+o(1)} when |F_pi|<=N^{f+o(1)}.
Compare with a claimed lower-bound certificate C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}. If rho<1+epsilon, q+alpha_ad<1+epsilon, and f<epsilon, the transcript contradicts its own target claim.

For rows not in F_pi and not parity-bound, apply the odd private-row perturbation. Acceptance is invariant in the occurrence-local model but D_pi(x) flips, so the transcript is a semantic spoof rather than a valid certificate.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a conditional route-level cap and a restricted-model spoof test, not P != NP and not a full EF+SAT_U no-go. The unresolved formal point is the exact Psys rule ledger: semantic binding must be syntactic and advice-free, otherwise ForcedRows is not yet valid.

assumptions: Model is the restricted occurrence-local proof system EF+SAT_U^{occ}; full EF+SAT_U is not covered unless complete-row forcing is extractable from real formula syntax.
The generator G_N is uniform, has overhead N^{rho+o(1)}, and emits SAT instances of length polylog(N) in a beta-zero XOR family with M_N<=N^{q+o(1)} queries per row.
The adaptive cover for pi has exponent alpha_ad=max{tau,max_l(a_l+mu_l),max_l omega_l} and supplies all labels needed by D_pi without advice-selected hard rows.
Row-parity binding is assumed outside F_pi: for every x notin F_pi, the transcript syntactically certifies D_pi(x)=H_N^SAT(x) without circular reference to the target lower bound.
Patch circuits are unrestricted Boolean circuits in the same size measure used by the claimed beta-zero lower bound.
This is a route-level falsifier theorem; it is not a proof of P != NP.
definitions: source object: an EF+SAT_U^{occ} transcript pi for H_N^SAT(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_N(x,j)), with occurrence labels y_{x,j} and an adaptive label-cover profile alpha_ad.

target object: a scoped route no-go theorem saying low-cover proof-mediated beta-zero XOR certificates cannot validly certify C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} unless they force at least N^{epsilon-o(1)} complete rows.

controlled interface: the parser pi -> (Q_pi,D_pi,F_pi) outputs the touched occurrence object Q_pi, the low-cover row-parity decoder D_pi(x)=xor_j a_pi(x,j), and ForcedRows F_pi requiring explicit semantic patching.

target-preserving condition: the parser, decoder, and patch construction are uniform or advice-free except for hardwiring the fixed falsifying transcript in the negative direction, and all circuit upper bounds stay in the same unrestricted Boolean circuit model as the claimed lower bound.
ForcedRows F_pi are syntactically identified rows whose semantic parity is not supplied by the low-cover decoder under the parser's row-parity binding rules.
A sparse-row patch for F_pi is an unrestricted circuit that computes D_pi off F_pi and hardwires corrected row behavior on F_pi.

equations.label: forced-row-threshold

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If ForcedRows has exponent f<epsilon and the low-cover/parity-binding hypotheses hold, the certificate produces a same-model circuit below the claimed threshold; if parity binding cannot be proved, the transcript is only locally sound and is rejected by a spoof falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Main conditional theorem packet for the proof-delivery queue: it reduces the row-forcing lower bound to a parser lemma plus row-parity binding outside ForcedRows.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Occurrence-local forced-row cap: let Psys=EF+SAT_U^{occ} and let an accepted beta-zero XOR transcript pi parse to an advice-free low-cover row decoder D_pi and a syntactic forced-row set F_pi. If D_pi(x)=H_N^SAT(x) for all rows x notin F_pi, C(D_pi)<=N^{max{rho,q+alpha_ad}+o(1)}, and |F_pi|<=N^{f+o(1)}, then C(H_N^SAT)<=N^{max{rho,q+alpha_ad,1+f}+o(1)}. Thus any valid certificate claiming C(H_N^SAT)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} with rho,q+alpha_ad<1+epsilon must have f>=epsilon-o(1), or it is refuted by a sparse-row patch falsifier.

assumptions: Rules of EF+SAT_U^{occ} inspect only occurrence labels and explicitly declared local clauses; they do not invoke global SAT semantics except through parser-marked semantic clauses.
The tested row x has no parser-marked row-parity binding clause and no global equality clause tying its private labels to shared formula semantics.
The flip is odd on the labels contributing to D_pi(x), so it changes the row parity but preserves all even/check-local constraints not involving a semantic binding rule.
definitions: source object: an accepted occurrence-local transcript pi with private labels y_{x,j} attached to occurrences G_N(x,j).
target object: a countermodel to using local consistency as a valid semantic certificate for beta-zero row parity.
controlled interface: the observable is the acceptance predicate of pi under assignments to occurrence labels and the decoded parity D_pi(x).
target-preserving condition: the perturbation changes only private occurrence labels and does not alter the fixed generator, query schedule, or proof syntax outside the tested row.

equations.label: odd-private-flip
equations.valid_when: Valid when the chosen occurrence label is private to row x and is not protected by a semantic binding clause.

equations.label: parity-change
equations.valid_when: Applies when D_pi is the XOR of row labels and the perturbation flips an odd number of contributing labels.

equations.label: local-acceptance-invariance
equations.valid_when: Requires every checked rule touching the flipped labels to be occurrence-local and invariant under the selected private flip.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The lemma fails exactly when a rule reads real SAT formula semantics, identifies shared formula occurrences globally, or contains an explicit row-parity binding clause; those failures become parser obligations rather than proof progress.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Countermodel sublemma showing why the live theorem must prove row-parity binding, not merely ordinary local soundness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Private occurrence-label perturbation falsifier: for a row x not syntactically protected by row-parity binding, an odd flip of private occurrence labels preserves every occurrence-local rule of EF+SAT_U^{occ} while changing the decoded row parity. Therefore local soundness alone cannot justify D_pi(x)=H_N^SAT(x); the row must enter F_pi or the system must expose a nonlocal semantic rule.

assumptions: Transcript syntax is explicit enough to identify labels belonging to row x and to distinguish local clauses from SAT-semantic clauses.
Adaptive cover summaries have declared parameters tau,a_l,mu_l,omega_l that can be charged in the circuit upper-bound ledger.
A row is forced only if the parser finds a syntactic semantic certificate that blocks every odd private-row perturbation for that row.

controlled interface: parsing separates local occurrence constraints, adaptive cover openings, and semantic parity-binding clauses.
